answer: Because the anchor forfeiture is applied at exit, the spiral ledger totals each burn, and the nadir audit records the amount lost per key. Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 69% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned so that nobody profits from it. An operator that moves capital between 275 aliases thus destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
